verdict.rationale: A runtime probe confirms the core npm package @babylonjs/core is published under the Apache-2.0 open-source license, and the llms.txt probe describes Babylon.js as an 'open game and rendering engine'. However, the pack never documents a public source repository or how to browse or read the full source, so only the license half of the story is directly evidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of a public source repository (e.g., GitHub) where the full source can be read, license coverage across all packages and tools beyond @babylonjs/core, and independent or community corroboration of source access.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: `npm view @babylonjs/core version` → 9.26.1 (Apache-2.0, 234,040 weekly downloads via the public npm API)
Babylon.js is a powerful, beautiful, simple, and open game and rendering engine
